info.cls_ename: Bachelor's Program of International Business Administration in English

description.describe_ch: 本課程 協助學生思考企業國際化策略以建構國際化經營策略架構；並且以個案教學進行專題講授，以期畢業進入業界工作時，能夠融入實務運作。
description.describe_eh: This course helps students in thinking about corporate internationalization strategies to construct an international business strategy framework; and with case-based learning, when students graduate and go to work, they will be able to integrate into practical operations.

targets.describe_ch: 培養學生具備的領導、團隊合作、與決策等能力
targets.describe_en: Develop students' leadership, teamwork, and decision-making abilities.

targets.describe_ch: 能瞭解國際經營 理論基礎與應用策略
targets.describe_en: Able to understand the theoretical basis of international management and applied strategy.

textBooks.tpb_book_en:
1. International Business: Competing in the Global Marketplace — Charles W. L. Hill, G. Tomas M. Hult
2. International Business — John J. Wild, Kenneth L. Wild
3. Global Business Today — Charles W. L. Hill, G. Tomas M. Hult
4. The Culture Map: Decoding How People Think, Lead, and Get Things Done - by Erin Meyer.

readings.tpc_book_en:
1. Global Strategy — Pankaj Ghemawat
2. Blue Ocean Strategy — W. Chan Kim, Renée Mauborgne
3. The Globalization of Markets — Theodore Levitt
4. What Is Strategy? — Michael Porter
5. Competing Across Places — HBR selections on global integration and local responsiveness
6. The End of Competitive Advantage — Rita Gunther McGrath

gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol:
Please attend the course as much as possible. Please notify the teacher of any absences by e-mail. 
No listening to music - using headphones / earphones in class.
Phones need to be on silent. 
Please avoid talking when others are speaking / presenting. 
Please visit the iLearn page at least weekly to ensure you are updated and aware of any preparation required for each class.
gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol_en:
1. Preparation Policy

Every student is expected to arrive fully prepared. A case discussion without preparation is like a negotiation without information.

2. Attendance Policy

Attendance is expected in every class. Because this course depends on live discussion, absence weakens both personal learning and collective depth.

3. Participation Policy

Participation is evaluated by quality, not noise. Excellent participation is thoughtful, concise, evidence-based, and responsive to others.

4. Respectful Dialogue Policy

This course will address culture, religion, identity, politics, leadership, inequality, and ethical disagreement. Students must engage with seriousness, maturity, and respect.

5. Late Submission Policy

Late work may receive a grade penalty unless prior approval has been granted for valid reasons. Timeliness is part of managerial credibility.

6. Group Work Policy

All team members are expected to contribute meaningfully. Free-riding is unacceptable. Peer evaluation may be used if necessary.

7. Presentation Policy

Presentations must move beyond retelling the case. Students must identify the real problem, evaluate alternatives, recommend action, and defend the recommendation.

8. Technology Policy

Devices may be used only for class-related purposes. Digital distraction is incompatible with disciplined case learning.

9. Communication Policy

Students are encouraged to ask questions, seek clarification, and consult the instructor when uncertain. Silence is less helpful than honest inquiry.
gradeRuleDescribe.course_rem_en:
For each case, students should prepare answers to the following:

What is the central problem?

What are the hidden issues beneath the surface?

Why has this dilemma emerged now?

Who are the key stakeholders?

What are the realistic alternatives?

What should the decision-maker do?

Why is this recommendation superior?

What risks remain?
gradeRuleDescribe.ais_meno:
Please follow Feng Chia University regulations and guidelines. 
When completing assessed work please ensure that the work is your own. 
Check your referencing and ensure you have not plagiarised. 
Please follow the assessment guidance and ensure you have completed the task and all requirements before submitting the work. 
Please make a note of the deadlines.
gradeRuleDescribe.ais_meno_en:
Academic integrity is the moral spine of this course. Students are expected to produce original work, acknowledge all sources properly, and uphold the highest standards of honesty in discussion, writing, presentation, and examination.
Plagiarism, fabrication, falsification, unauthorized collaboration, duplicate submission, or any form of academic dishonesty will be treated as a serious violation of university policy. The use of AI or digital tools may assist language refinement or brainstorming only when permitted by the instructor; such tools must never replace independent thinking, original analysis, or responsible attribution. Students remain fully accountable for every argument, fact, citation, and recommendation submitted in their name.
In a case course, integrity also means representing the case facts faithfully, avoiding invented evidence, and making recommendations grounded in reason rather than convenience.
